reasoning_notes.reasoning: With no history, choose a positive margin while remaining competitive; 10 earns 10 if C bids lower, and half the surplus if tied.
With no history and symmetric firms, choose a middle wage to balance winning labor against margin.
Undercut the tie by the smallest increment to capture the full unit while retaining 10.5 profit.
A tie at 10 earned 5. A small increase wins the unit for 9.5 profit; undercutting would concede labor.
C raised to 10.5 after our tie at 10. Matching 10.5 splits labor for 9.5 profit; undercutting by 0.5 earns 10, so choose 10.
A earned nothing last round and may undercut my 10.5 wage. At 10, I can win if A stays at 9.5 or tie if A matches; raising further risks losing labor, while undercutting A leaves little margin.
C returned to 10 after winning with 10.5; tie at 10 splits labor profitably, while raising risks losing the whole unit.
A matched 10 last round after my 10.5 win. Repeating 10.5 wins if A stays at 10, while the extra wage costs nothing if A also chooses 10.5 and we split.
C has repeatedly chosen 10 or 10.5. Offering 10.5 secures the unit if C stays at 10, while a tie still earns 4.75; a higher offer would reduce profit further.
A matched 10 after my 10.5 offer, then stayed at 10 while I won at 10.5. Repeating 10.5 preserves the profitable winning offer and avoids splitting labor at 10.
The recent tie and higher offer suggest C may stay at 10.5. Matching preserves a chance at half the labor while avoiding a costly overbid; a lower wage would lose for sure.
A matched 10.5 last round, so matching preserves half the labor at a strong margin. Raising costs more per unit; lowering would likely lose the pool.
Matching the recent 10.5 offers preserves half the labor at a positive margin; raising risks sacrificing profit if C matches.
Matching A’s repeated 10.5 preserves half the labor and earns 4.75; raising sacrifices margin, while undercutting is unnecessary if A stays put.
C has matched 10.5 for three rounds; matching preserves half the labor at a positive margin, while raising risks needless margin loss and undercutting earns less if C stays put.
Matching the recent tie preserves half the labor share at a strong margin; raising risks giving away profit, while undercutting sacrifices margin without evidence A will do so.
Matching the repeated 10.5 offer preserves half the labor at a 4.75 profit if C does the same, while avoiding a costly bidding escalation.
Keep the tie and earn 4.75; undercutting to 10 earns only 5 if A stays at 10.5, but risks a matching response and lower profit.
Matching C’s repeated 10.5 offer secures half the labor for 4.75 profit; undercutting sacrifices margin, while raising risks earning nothing.
A has matched 10.5 for five straight rounds, so matching preserves a half share at a 9.5 margin. Raising risks sacrificing profit; undercutting gives away margin without evidence A will move lower.
